title: C-section
what: Surgery to deliver the baby through a cut in the lower belly. It is usually done with a shot in the back, so you are awake.
why: When a vaginal birth is risky for the mother or the baby. It can be planned or urgent.
duration: surgery usually takes 40 to 60 minutes; the hospital stay is usually 3 to 5 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor decides what to do
Heart disease, blood pressure problems, or diabetes
If you had belly surgery or a C-section before
If you had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Tests and an exam. The hospital will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you and explain the pain relief.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Before a planned surgery, usually no food from the evening before. The hospital will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: A hospital bag for you and the baby, postpartum underwear, and a support belt if your doctor advises it.

steps: An IV is put into a vein and a thin tube into your bladder
The anesthesiologist gives a shot in your back. Your legs and belly go numb
A screen is put up in front of you
The doctor makes a cut in the lower belly and lifts out the baby
You are shown your baby, and the doctor closes the cut
You are moved to a recovery room
feel: During surgery: pressure and movement, but no pain
Sometimes nausea or chills. Tell the anesthesiologist
After surgery, the cut hurts. You will get pain medicine
after: You are usually helped to get up within the first day. This is important
For a few weeks, do not lift anything heavier than your baby
Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own. The doctor will tell you
red_flags: Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad in an hour
A fever over 38 degrees, or redness or pus on the cut
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or one swollen leg: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have a vaginal birth after a C-section?
faq.a: Often yes. It depends on the scar and the past surgery. You decide together with your doctor.

faq.q: How soon can I get up after a C-section?
faq.a: Usually within the first day, with help from a nurse. Getting up early helps you recover.

faq.q: Can I breastfeed after a C-section?
faq.a: Yes. The hospital chooses medicines that are safe for breastfeeding.

reminders.text: Planned C-section tomorrow. Pack your bag, pregnancy records, and ID. Eat only until the time the hospital gave you.
